profile.reading: The registry operator name Centersquare and the domain centersquaredc.com resolve, via a same brand redirect, to csquare.com, indicating Centersquare and Csquare are current names for the same operator; this registry separately lists a Csquare operator record as well. The operator own site states it runs 80 colocation data centers across 30 markets, totaling 3.5 million square feet of space and more than 500 megawatts of power capacity, serving over 2,000 customers and more than 200 network and technology service providers, and describes itself as having operated for over 20 years, implying founding in the early 2000s. Its confirmed markets include Northern Virginia, Chicago Illinois, Phoenix Arizona, the Dallas Fort Worth area of Texas, Seattle Washington, the New York and New Jersey metro area, and Atlanta Georgia, matching every state where this registry carries a Centersquare facility. The company is headquartered at 3100 Olympus Boulevard, Suite 510, Coppell, Texas. No detailed founding history, prior company names, ownership structure, or building specific address and MW figures for this particular row were confirmed in available sourcing this session.
profile.research_note: Centersquare and Csquare appear to be the same current operator (centersquaredc.com redirects to csquare.com); this registry carries both as separate operator records (Centersquare 17 facilities, Csquare 7 facilities). reading.body:
Centersquare's IAD4 campus publishes 238.7 MW of combined utility power across 269,000 square feet of technical space. The spec page lists combined utility power rather than IT load, so the usable IT figure is not published. If combined utility power approximates IT load, and assuming 40 kW per rack as a common AI training density, 238.7 MW would support roughly 5,968 racks, calculated as 238,700 kW divided by 40 kW. That assumption is not Centersquare's claim, and the true IT load is likely lower once power, cooling, and overhead losses are accounted for. The 269,000 square feet of technical space is large enough to host dense compute at scale, though floor loading and cooling topology are not published.

The five certifications address audit and compliance readiness in distinct ways. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 qualify the campus for workloads where financial controls and trust-service criteria must be independently verified. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data environments. ISO 27001 establishes a certified information security management framework. NIST 800-53 alignment qualifies the campus to support US federal and regulated workloads that require that control baseline. Taken together, the certification stack covers the compliance surface area most common in enterprise and government AI deployments.

Within Virginia, IAD4 sits outside the ranked set this site has read. Virginia has 326 facilities mapped, but only 20 of those have published megawatt figures, and those 20 facilities account for a combined 1,338.6 MW. IAD4's 238.7 MW figure places it twenty-first by published MW among Virginia facilities this site has read, meaning it falls just beyond the tracked group rather than inside it. Virginia's concentration of published capacity in a small fraction of mapped facilities reflects how few operators publish power figures at all, so the 1,338.6 MW total understates the state's true installed base.
